title: Cloud Marketplace Refresh — Kickoff Notes (AWS + GCP)
linked_artifacts: Slack: #docs thread 1769395510 (security packet public vs gated)
content:
Doc owner: Chris Osei (Product Ops)  |  Working notes  |  Please add comments inline.

Meeting: Cloud Marketplace Refresh — Kickoff
Date/time: 2026-01-08 (PT)
Attendees (partial): Jordan Blake, Camila Reyes, Soojin Lee, Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer, Naomi Feldman, Dr. Aisha Rahman (partial), Alex Martinez, Elliot Price, Priya Natarajan, Chloe Martin, Cole Summers, Markus Klein, Laura Bennett

Goal of kickoff
- Align on outcomes, scope, and owners across: listings + SKUs/packaging + security packet + onboarding/metering.
- Confirm what “done” means for AWS + GCP submissions (and what can ship post-listing).
- Identify risks early (approval cycles, SKU changes/back-compat, security wording, entitlement delays).

Context (why now)
- Current marketplace listings are legacy positioning and don’t map cleanly to current product surface area (Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons).
- Procurement-led customers are explicitly asking for marketplace purchase paths; sales cycle slows when listing/SKUs/security packet aren’t aligned.
- Current onboarding via marketplace has avoidable friction: entitlement propagation, org linking edge cases, unclear “what happens next.”

Non-goals (for this iteration)
- No major re-architecture of billing pipeline. We’ll do minimal schema changes required for SKU mapping + metering identifiers.
- No net-new compliance certification commitments in marketplace text (must stay within verified posture).
- No promise of on-prem for all customers via marketplace self-serve; Private is sales-assisted if required.

Agenda
1) Success metrics + target audiences (PLG vs procurement-led) (10m)
2) Packaging/SKUs: what we’re selling on marketplace and how it meters (20m)
3) Security packet: what we need for AWS/GCP review + what goes public (20m)
4) Onboarding flow: subscription → entitlement → org provisioning → first API key → metering/invoicing (20m)
5) Risks/assumptions + timeline draft (15m)
6) Next steps + working cadence (5m)

1) Success metrics + audiences
Primary audiences
- Procurement-led enterprise buyers: want predictable contract vehicle, invoices via AWS/GCP, security packet, and support clarity.
- Product/engineering teams: want “time-to-first-token” low friction and confidence in performance/cost controls.

Proposed success metrics (v1)
- Conversion: marketplace listing view → subscribe (baseline TBD; Ben to pull baseline sheet)
- Median time-to-first-success (first successful API call) from subscription: target < 20 minutes for Hosted; Dedicated/Private target “same day initial access + SLA’d provisioning expectations.”
- Drop-off rate at key steps: entitlement validation errors, org linking failures, API key creation incomplete.
- Support burden: reduction in provisioning-delay tickets; track entitlement sync latency distribution.

Open question
- Do we optimize first for AWS (higher pipeline) vs parallel AWS+GCP? Current plan: parallel where possible; sequencing for partner review may differ.

2) Packaging/SKUs — initial proposal
Principle: SKUs must map 1:1 (or many:1 with clear rules) to internal billing meters + be legible to buyers.

SKU families (draft)
- Hosted API (usage-based): per-token + per-embedding units; include standard support.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved capacity dimension(s) aligned to GPU pools; predictable throughput; SLA-backed.
- Private (VPC / on-prem options): platform fee + support tier; sales-assisted procurement; may still be transacted via marketplace private offer.
- Add-ons: compliance pack (longer log retention, premium audit export), advanced observability retention, premium SLA.

Key decisions needed
- Naming conventions must be consistent across AWS and GCP constraints (character limits, allowed separators).
- Minimum commitments / floor pricing: finance guardrails for public offer vs private offer.
- Trial/credits: allow limited-time trial on hosted? If yes, ensure no conflict with internal free credits.

Owners
- SKU catalog finalization: Soojin Lee + Laura Bennett (Finance) + Cole Summers (billing mapping)
- Marketplace offer structure constraints: Stephanie Nguyen (AWS) + Lukas Meyer (GCP) + Partnerships ops

Open questions (packaging)
- Hosted: Do we expose token dimensions separately by model tier (e.g., “standard vs premium models”) or keep single token meter and handle model differences as internal price book only?
- Dedicated: How do we represent throughput guarantees in listing without overcommitting? (language + SLA attachment?)
- Private: What is the cleanest marketplace packaging for Private that doesn’t confuse “Private deployment” vs “Dedicated capacity”?

3) Security packet — what’s required + publication plan
What AWS/GCP typically look for (high-level)
- Data flow overview (what data is processed, stored, where)
- Encryption in transit/at rest + key management options (KMS/HSM integrations where applicable)
- Audit logging: what events, retention, export, customer access
- Retention/residency defaults and customer-configurable settings
- Shared responsibility model (what Redwood controls vs customer controls)
- Compliance posture: SOC 2 / ISO-aligned controls, plus how to request reports (don’t publish restricted evidence publicly)

Draft approach
- Public docs site: “Marketplace Security Overview” + “Data handling & retention summary” + “Audit logs overview” with careful wording.
- Gated / on request: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, vendor risk artifacts (distributed via secure process).

Owners
- Security packet content owner: Naomi Feldman + Olga Petrov
- Review/wording approval: Dr. Aisha Rahman + Sofia Mendes (counsel) (as needed for claims)
- Docs publication: Alex Martinez + Elliot Price

Open questions (security)
- What security artifacts are mandatory attachments in AWS vs GCP portals vs just linked URLs?
- What is our official stance on training data usage in marketplace copy (must match product policy exactly; avoid ambiguous phrasing)?
- Can we commit to specific retention defaults publicly without locking ourselves out of product flexibility? (proposal: publish “defaults + configurable range,” avoid absolute language)

4) Onboarding flow — subscription to first call
Current pain points (from Sales/Support anecdotes)
- Entitlement propagation delays: customer subscribes, Redwood console says “not entitled yet.”
- Existing Redwood orgs: confusion on whether to create new org vs link existing.
- Multi-subscription edge cases: one company with multiple AWS accounts / projects.
- Unclear next steps after subscription; docs and console not aligned.

Target flow (v1)
1) Customer subscribes in AWS/GCP Marketplace
2) Customer is redirected to Redwood Console “Marketplace onboarding” entrypoint
3) Console checks entitlement (provider + account/project id)
4) Customer chooses: create new org OR link to existing org
5) Console provisions org entitlements/limits + creates first API key
6) Customer runs quickstart request (copy-paste) and sees success
7) Metering: internal mapping ensures usage is billed via marketplace dimensions; show “billing source = marketplace” in console

Engineering items (high-level)
- Entitlement verification endpoints + error codes
- Harden entitlement sync job (retries, idempotency, alerting)
- Metering dimension mapping correctness + reconciliation
- Console UX: clear error states + retry guidance + support link
- Telemetry events across funnel

Owners
- Console onboarding entrypoint: Chloe Martin
- Entitlement verification + sync job: Ethan Park / platform team (Priya sponsor)
- Metering dimension mapping: Cole Summers + Nadia Rahman
- Funnel telemetry: Ben Carter + Nadia Rahman
- QA / E2E test plan: Leila Farouk

Open questions (onboarding)
- What’s our promised SLA/expectation for entitlement propagation? (We need language for docs/FAQ.)
- What’s the support escalation path if entitlement is delayed beyond threshold?
- How do we handle customers who subscribe but already have direct-contract billing enabled? (block? allow but choose billing source?)

5) Timeline draft (6–8 weeks target)
Week 1: Discovery & requirements
- Confirm AWS + GCP listing constraints, portal requirements, security checklist
- Finalize target SKUs and draft internal→marketplace meter mapping

Week 2–3: Draft assets + cross-functional review
- Listing copy (AWS + GCP) + FAQ draft
- Security packet draft (public + gated plan)
- Initial screenshots/diagram checklist

Week 3–5: Engineering enablement + docs
- Implement entitlement verification API + console onboarding entrypoint
- Metering dimension mapping updates; reconciliation plan
- Add telemetry for onboarding funnel
- Publish onboarding docs + security overview pages

Week 5–6: Partner submission + iteration
- Submit AWS listing + artifacts; address feedback
- Submit GCP listing + artifacts; address feedback

Week 6–8: Launch readiness
- Enablement for Sales/CS/Support
- Internal announcement, escalation playbook, dashboard monitoring

Risks / dependencies
- AWS/GCP review cycles are unpredictable; we need buffer.
- SKU changes must avoid breaking existing marketplace customers; migration strategy required (or keep legacy SKUs live temporarily).
- Security claims must be consistent across docs, listing, and questionnaire responses.
- Billing dimension mismatch risk → customer trust risk; prioritize integration test coverage.

Working cadence
- Weekly core sync (Partnerships + PMM + Product + Eng + Security + Docs): 30 min
- Async updates via tracker doc + Linear umbrella ticket
- Partner review tracker maintained by Partnerships ops

Action items (initial)
- Chris Osei: create single project tracker + RACI; link Linear umbrella (PM-1843) and keep owners updated.
- Soojin Lee: circulate SKU catalog v2 proposal for final comments; identify open points requiring exec decision.
- Camila Reyes: confirm listing messaging pillars and “do/don’t” language; start copy blocks draft.
- Naomi Feldman: outline security packet table of contents + what’s public vs gated; schedule compliance review.
- Chloe Martin: confirm console UX requirements + edge-case states; coordinate with Eng on API contract.
- Cole Summers: propose internal meter identifiers + mapping strategy for AWS/GCP dimensions; flag any schema changes needed.
- Ben Carter: pull baseline funnel metrics + identify instrumentation gaps.

Notes to self (Chris)
- Keep this doc “messy but current.” Once decisions settle, move finalized content to Confluence and keep Drive for working drafts.
- Ensure we capture: (1) what customers see in marketplace listing, (2) what they see in console, (3) what Support sees when something breaks.
